analysis: The PR changes only docs/operations/provider-release.md (head lines ~315-318). It replaces a sentence claiming that local builds, tests and qualify-sdk retain production defaults with a statement that qualify-sdk sets DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod, so its tests see production defaults on every branch, and that on the dev branch an unset value compiles the dev identity (provider-swift/Package.swift). This is documentation only. It changes no code, workflow, signing, secret handling, attestation, or authorization behavior, so none of the threat model's trust boundaries or controls (TB-002, TB-011, A-010, A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054) are weakened. The new text discloses build-environment selection behavior and does not expose secrets. The claim describes a CI/Package.swift behavior that is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it. Open integration questions are limited to whether Package.swift and the qualify-sdk workflow actually match the description, and whether an unset env on the dev branch could compile a dev-identity artifact in a place that is expected to be production. That is a documentation-accuracy question and does not establish a security regression. No threat-model update is needed.
